Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

care verb

about something

also care about, I don’t care, what do I care?, I don’t go for, I don’t give a hoot, I couldn’t care less, I don’t give a damn, I’m interested in that, no sweat (it doesn’t bother me), I don’t give a darn, what’s it to me?, I don’t care to say more, I don’t really care as long as, I don’t mind that, I don’t mind, I don’t care for her, I like (it is dear to me)

classical

Plaut. Most. 627: nōn ego istuc cūrō quī sit quid sit unde sit
Cic. N. D. 2.167: magna dī cūrant, parva neglegunt
Traupman 94: Ista nōn cūrō.
Traupman 103: I don’t mind that …, nōn cūrō quod (+ indic.)
Traupman 287

cūrō, cūrāre, cūrāvī, cūrātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

care about

With an accusative or a question; with a negative it is “I don’t care”: nōn cūrō, nihil cūrō.

Other words

  • cūrae esse — be a concern (to someone), matter

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: multīs est cūrae; Caes. BG 1.33 (Lewis & Short): sibi eam rem cūrae futūram; Traupman 101: id mihi cūrae est; Traupman 334

    With a dative of the person: mihi cūrae est, I care about it, I’ll see to it.

  • labōrō, labōrāre, labōrāvī, labōrātum — be concerned, be bothered

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.3: nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs; Traupman 108: nōn labōrō, for “no sweat”; Cic. Rosc. Am. 97: cujus manū sit percussus, nōn labōrō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 103: I don’t mind if …, nōn labōrō sī … · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    With dē and the ablative, or ut and the subjunctive; nōn labōrō, it doesn’t trouble me (Lewis & Short).

  • nīl (nihil) moror — I don’t care for, I can do without

    also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.15.16 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 94: nīl moror (+ acc.); Traupman 99; Traupman 322 · Wiktionary

    With an accusative; Lewis & Short: “to care nothing about it”. Nōn moror is also “I don’t mind” (see mind, object).

  • floccī nōn faciō — I don’t give a hoot about

    floccī, genitive of value (“at a tuft of wool”), with facere · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 3.5.3: ego, quae tū loquere, floccī nōn faciō (Lewis & Short), s.v. floccus; Cic. Att. 13.50.3: nec tamen floccī faciō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 100: eum floccī nōn faciō; Traupman 300; Traupman 329

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut.; Cic. in epistulīs)

  • floccī nōn facere — not care a straw for, not give a darn about

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.15.4: tōtam rem pūblicam floccī nōn facere (Lewis & Short s.v. floccus); Traupman 96

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut.; Cic. in epistulīs)

    A genitive of value: “to reckon at a tuft of wool”.

  • Quid meā? — what’s it to me?

    also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 4.5.45 (Lewis & Short s.v. cōnfugiō); Traupman 94; Traupman 287

    Meā is the form used with rēfert and interest: “what (does it matter) to me?”

  • mihi cordī est — I care for, I like, it is dear to me

    cordī, dative of cor, with esse and a dative of the person · also used · classical · Plaut. Cist. 1.1.110: utut ergā mē est meritus, mihi cordī est tamen (Lewis & Short s.v. cor); Cic. Lael. 15: idque eō mihi magis est cordī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 287

    “I don’t care for her” is nōn est mihi cordī. Traupman’s ea meō cordī nōn cāra est mixes this idiom with cārus and the possessive meus; we have found no classical instance of that shape.

Examples

  • Nōn ego istuc cūrō quī sit quid sit unde sit

    I don’t care who he is, what he is or where he comes from.Plaut. Most. 627

  • nūllā in rē jam tē festīnāre volō; nihil labōrō, nisi ut salvus sīs

    I don’t want you to hurry over anything now; all I care about is that you get well.Cic. Fam. 16.4.3

  • magna dī cūrant, parva neglegunt

    The gods care about great things and neglect the small ones.Cic. N. D. 2.167

  • Nōn labōrō.

    It doesn’t bother me (Traupman’s “no sweat”).Traupman 108

  • Id nōn faciō floccī.

    I don’t give a darn about that.Traupman 96

  • nōn libet mihi dēplōrāre vītam

    I don’t care to bemoan my lifeCic. Sen. 84 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōn libet plūra dīcere.

    I don’t care to say more.Traupman 94

  • Meā nīl rēfert, dum …

    I don’t really care, as long as …Traupman 287

  • meā quidem istuc nihil rēfert

    that makes no difference to me, at any ratePlaut. Pers. 4.3.68 (Lewis & Short s.v. rēfert)

See also it makes no difference, never mind, care, mind, concern.
